content: Security is an illusion. The desire for security and the feeling of insecurity are the same thing.
author: Alan Watts
sourceWork: The Book: On the Taboo Against Knowing Who You Are (1966)
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Courage is rarely the thunderous heroics we see in movies; it is the quiet voice at the end of the day that says, 'I will try again tomorrow.' When we wait to feel completely fearless before taking a step, we stay trapped in place.

In Alan Watts's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Real strength shows up with a racing pulse and trembling hands. It is the willingness to be vulnerable, to risk looking foolish, and to stand up for what matters even when everything in you wants to hide.
reflectionPrompt: Where in your current routine are you choosing convenient illusion over uncomfortable truth?
